2608.13684.title: Learning to Assemble Novel Structures with Unfamiliar Parts under Semantic Constraints
2608.13684.paper_summary: This paper describes a neurosymbolic architecture for learning to assemble novel structures using evidence from embodied conversations and task demonstrations. We focus on scenarios where an agent encounters, after deployment, semantic constraints on structures--in other words, constraints as to which part types and features make valid structures--that were not available during training, and where it is initially unaware of the relevant structure and component part concepts. The agent must acquire and exploit such knowledge through user interactions while attempting assembly. We study this setting in a simulated toy truck assembly domain, learning from symbolic evidence encoded in natural language and from dense visual observations. Our experiments show that communicating semantic constraints through natural language (e.g., "dump trucks have a dumper") yields more data-efficient online adaptation than relying only on task demonstrations and/or only naming the parts through natural language.
2608.13684.paper_summary_zh: 這篇論文描述了一種神經符號架構，用於學習如何利用具身對話和任務示範中的證據來組裝新結構。<lb/>我們專注於這樣的情境：在部署後，代理遇到對結構的語義限制——換句話說，對哪些部件類型和特徵構成有效結構的限制——這些限制在訓練期間並不可用，且代理最初對相關結構和組件概念並不知情。<lb/>代理必須通過用戶互動來獲取和利用這些知識，同時嘗試進行組裝。<lb/>我們在一個模擬的玩具卡車組裝領域研究這一設置，從用自然語言編碼的符號證據和密集的視覺觀察中學習。<lb/>我們的實驗表明，通過自然語言傳達語義限制（例如，“自卸卡車有一個卸料器”）比僅依賴任務示範和/或僅用自然語言命名部件更能有效地進行在線適應。
